<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is a Python client library (“instagrapi”) providing an unofficial wrapper for Instagram’s private Web & Mobile APIs.  
   - It offers core features (login, media upload/download, direct messaging, insights, challenge resolution, 2FA) via a modular mixin design.  
   - It includes documentation (MkDocs), examples, tests, Dockerized development & CI/CD workflows, and plugins for docs.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   Top-level directories:  
     • instagrapi/ – the core library  
       • config.py, exceptions.py, extractors.py, image_util.py, utils.py, zones.py  
       • mixins/ – one module per IG feature (account, media, direct, story, etc.)  
       • types.py – data models for API responses  
       • story.py – StoryBuilder sub-system  
     • docs/ – MkDocs site source, usage-guide, best practices  
     • examples/ – standalone scripts demonstrating library usage  
     • tests.py – basic test suite  
     • util/ – MkDocs plugins (redirects, type-alias patch)  
     • docker/ + docker-compose.yml – dev/test environment  
     • .github/ – GitHub Actions workflows and custom actions (install deps, publish docs)  
     • setup.py, requirements*.txt – packaging & dependencies  

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - Describes two API modes (Web vs Mobile) with auto-selection to avoid limits  
   - Highlights the “Challenge Resolver” subsystem (Email/SMS handlers, 2FA TOTP)  
   - Lists major resource types (User, Media, Comment, Story, Hashtag, Location, Direct)  
   - Shows sample code leveraging the Client() + mixins + types  

4. How to create the system design diagram  
   a. Main components  
     1. Developer Application (your code or examples)  
     2. instagrapi Client Library  
        – Core: Session Manager, HTTP Transport, Config, Exceptions  
        – Mixin Modules: account, media, direct, story, comment, insight, etc.  
        – Data Models: types.py  
        – StoryBuilder: story.py  
        – Utilities: extractors, image_util, zones, utils  
        – Challenge Resolver: email/SMS handlers, TOTP  
     3. External Services  
        – Instagram Web API Endpoint  
        – Instagram Mobile API Endpoint  
        – Proxy Servers  
        – Email/SMS gateways (for challenge resolution)  
     4. Documentation Pipeline  
        – MkDocs + mkdocstrings + custom plugins (util/)  
        – GitHub Actions for building and publishing docs  
     5. CI/CD Pipeline  
        – Dockerized test environment (docker/ + docker-compose)  
        – GitHub Actions (code scanning, test, package, publish to PyPI)  
   b. Relationships & interactions  
     • Developer App invokes instagrapi.Client → Session Manager  
     • Session Manager uses HTTP Transport to send requests to Web or Mobile API  
     • Mixin modules call HTTP Transport with feature-specific endpoints  
     • Responses parsed into data models (types.py)  
     • Challenge Resolver intercepts 4xx/5xx, triggers Email/SMS flows via external gateways  
     • Optional TOTP generation for 2FA within library  
     • Documentation pipeline reads doc sources + code docstrings → MkDocs site → GitHub Pages  
     • CI/CD pipeline builds Docker image, runs tests, lints, type-checks, publishes package & docs  
   c. Architectural patterns & design principles  
     • Mixin pattern for modular per-feature endpoint implementations  
     • Separation of concerns: HTTP Transport vs business logic (mixins) vs data models  
     • Pluggable challenge resolution handlers  
     • Infrastructure as code: Docker, GitHub Actions, custom actions  
     • Documentation-as-code: MkDocs with plugins in util/  
   d. Relevant technologies & libraries  
     • Python ≥ 3.9, requests or httpx (HTTP layer)  
     • MkDocs, mkdocstrings, custom Python plugins (util/)  
     • Docker, docker-compose  
     • GitHub Actions (YAML workflows + custom actions)  
     • Twine, setuptools for packaging  

5. Guidelines for tailoring the diagram to this library project  
   - Emphasize core Client subsystem and how mixins extend it  
   - Show external dependencies (Instagram endpoints, proxies, email/SMS gateways)  
   - Visualize the docs & CI/CD pipelines—this is key for maintainers  
   - Do NOT show a database (none in this library)  
   - Focus on extensibility points: mixins folder, util plugins  

6. Elements to include in the diagram  
   - Clear component boxes labeled: Developer App, instagrapi Client (sub-boxes: Session, Transport, Mixins, Types, Utils, Challenge Resolver), External APIs/Services, Docs Pipeline, CI/CD Pipeline  
   - Directional arrows:  
     • Developer → Client → HTTP Transport → Instagram Web/Mobile APIs  
     • HTTP errors → Challenge Resolver → Email/SMS gateways → back to Client  
     • Codebase + docs → MkDocs → GitHub Actions → Published docs  
     • Codebase → Docker/Test → GitHub Actions → PyPI  
   - Color coding or shapes:  
     • Business logic (Client & mixins) in one color  
     • Infrastructure (Docker, CI/CD, Docs) in another  
     • External services in a third color  

By following these guidelines and mapping each folder or file cluster to a component in your diagram, you’ll capture the essential architecture of instagrapi while clearly showing data flows, modularity points, and operational pipelines. Don’t overthink it—separate the system into these logical components, label them clearly, and use arrows and colors to convey interactions.
